title: Multiwavelength classification supports new Omega Centauri binary candidates
summary: A cluster-adapted random forest helped identify candidate cataclysmic-variable counterparts in Omega Centauri. For newly proposed source 14e, the model favored this class with probability 0.59 alongside conventional optical and X-ray evidence. Candidate nature and counterpart association remain uncertain in the crowded field.
ai_technology: MUWCLASS random forest with feature-matched training subsets and Gaussian-process imputation
organization: George Washington University; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; IRAP

evidence.tested: Applied a training set assembled from 25 globular clusters to more than 200 Chandra sources, comparing class probabilities with conventional counterpart evidence. Source14e has six X-ray counts and a proposed blue optical counterpart.
evidence.unknown: Crowding, missing photometry and class imbalance limit labels. Proper motion and radio information are outside the classifier; background galaxies can be confused with binaries. Source14e photometry may be unreliable and identification is not confirmed. No new measured population count or dynamical mechanism is asserted.
evidence.ai_role: The trained classifier supplies candidate-specific class probabilities that guided the multiwavelength interpretation, rather than only providing a catalog or recovering known classes.

source_review.scope: Actual v1 classification procedure, source14e discussion/Table7 and training limitations; October22 v1 already contains result, November3 v2 metadata distinguished.
